title: What computer techs do

description: Computer repair technicians diagnose and fix desktops, laptops, and peripherals: hardware failures, malware, data recovery, upgrades, and networks. Certifications like CompTIA A+ open doors; reputation keeps them open.

title: Essential tools
d: Precision screwdriver set, spudgers, tweezers, anti-static wrist strap and mat, multimeter, USB boot drives (Windows, Linux, rescue), external drive dock, therm
description: Precision screwdriver set, spudgers, tweezers, anti-static wrist strap and mat, multimeter, USB boot drives (Windows, Linux, rescue), external drive dock, thermal paste, and compressed air. Pros add: POST card, soldering station, and a NAS for backups.

title: Key skills
d: Systematic diagnosis: isolate hardware vs software. OS reinstalls and driver wrangling. Malware removal. Data recovery basics (and knowing when to stop). Solder
description: Systematic diagnosis: isolate hardware vs software. OS reinstalls and driver wrangling. Malware removal. Data recovery basics (and knowing when to stop). Soldering for board-level work. Clear communication with non-technical customers.

title: Safety essentials
d: ESD protection: one zap kills boards. Power supply capacitors hold charge. Laptop batteries: handle swollen ones with extreme care (fire risk). Data privacy: cu
description: ESD protection: one zap kills boards. Power supply capacitors hold charge. Laptop batteries: handle swollen ones with extreme care (fire risk). Data privacy: customer data is sacred — never snoop, always protect.

title: Getting started
d: CompTIA A+ is the entry credential. Practice on old machines. Start with friends-and-family repairs, then a shop or on-site service. Specialize: data recovery,
description: CompTIA A+ is the entry credential. Practice on old machines. Start with friends-and-family repairs, then a shop or on-site service. Specialize: data recovery, business IT, or Mac repair each pay premiums.

title: Pro tips
d: Back up before touching anything — no exceptions. Document passwords and BitLocker keys. Test with known-good parts to isolate faults. Keep a library of drivers
description: Back up before touching anything — no exceptions. Document passwords and BitLocker keys. Test with known-good parts to isolate faults. Keep a library of drivers and installers. Honest timelines beat optimistic ones.
